title: Generated FIELDLIST body recovery profile
scope: Malformed FIELDLIST OBJECTS-body parser recovery and CLI disposition at six locally generated DWG revisions.

selection.source: P6-F typed OBJECTS parser and writer inventory
selection.reason: FIELDLIST has bounded typed parse/write routes, and no dedicated malformed-body CLI profile existed. The profile uses a single permitted null member so it does not claim a complete FIELD/FIELDLIST graph.

source.provenance: Generated from scratch by the in-tree dwg_local_roundtrip test writer and removed by the test runner.
source.profile: One FIELDLIST with a single null FIELD handle, followed by a LINE sentinel.
source.mutation: The generator searches the bounded FIELDLIST body for a one-bit change rejected by DRW_FieldList::parseDwg while preserving the common OBJECTS prologue and handle.

AC1027.output: strict and partial output refused by the existing source-reference gate

assertions: All six generated revisions continue through the following LINE and report one failed OBJECTS frame, zero entity parse failures, and balanced source/published/failed frame accounting.
At AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, and AC1032, strict ASCII/Binary conversion refuses atomically and explicit-partial ASCII/Binary output passes fresh DXF readback with the LINE retained.
At AC1027, strict and explicit-partial output preserve the destination and refuse at the existing source-reference gate.

validation.syntax: python3 -m py_compile tests/dwg2dxf_cli_contract_tests.py passed before the final receipt and plan edits.
validation.diff_check: git diff --check passed before the final receipt and plan edits.
validation.targeted: ctest --test-dir build-gcc -V -R '^dwg2dxf_cli_fieldlist_recovery$' passed 1/1 in 0.92 seconds and reported 28 controls.
validation.aggregate: The longer dwg2dxf_cli_partial_read_disposition aggregate was not rerun for this isolated selector slice.

limits: Generated parser recovery and CLI disposition only; FIELDLIST membership closure, FIELD evaluation semantics, producer-authored prevalence, and application recalculation are not qualified.
